newsitem.title: USA: Gulf Canada sees Clyde asset value rise.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada sees Clyde asset value rise.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd expects to raise the net asset value of its recent acquisition, Clyde Petroleum Plc, to the pruchase price of 120 pence per share by the end of this year from the current 90 pence per share, chief executive J.P. Bryan said Friday.

"We have a good chance to get NAV up to purchase price and we will do this from the 183 million barrels of reserves that Clyde currently classifies as non-commercial," he told FirstEnergy Capital's East Coast Canadian Energy Conference.
Bryant said he expects Gulf Canada to earn C$45 million, or $0.07 per share, this year, up from $37 million in 1996.
Sales volumes are expected to be 180,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, the executive said.
"We are going to turn this company into one with revenues of C$1 billion. Two years ago the only billion dollar thing we could talk about was the debt," Bryan said.
The company plans C$300 million of term debt which will come from Clyde, he said. "There is a flicker of hope that we can be investment grade," he said.
